title: Afghanistan to Host India in Historic T20I Series at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium
excerpt: The three-match series in September marks the first time Afghanistan will officially host India in international cricket, with all games played on Indian soil.
body:
• Afghanistan will officially "host" India for three T20 Internationals at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium in September, with matches tentatively set for September 13, 15, and 17.
  • The series marks the first time Afghanistan will host India in any bilateral cricket format, though all matches will be played on Indian soil.
  • Dates could shift if India's proposed tour to Bangladesh materializes, with the BCB hoping to stage matches from September 1 to 13.
  • The series provides crucial preparation for both squads ahead of the Asian Games, which begin September 24 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

Afghanistan will be the "home" side when they meet India in three Twenty20 Internationals in September, despite the series taking place at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium, both cricket boards confirmed on Tuesday, according to Reuters. The unusual arrangement marks the first time another country will officially host India on Indian soil.

A Historic Arrangement

Afghanistan have largely played their home fixtures in the United Arab Emirates and at Indian venues like Dehradun, Greater Noida, and Lucknow in recent years, with international sport yet to resume in the country due to security concerns following the Taliban's takeover in 2021. But they have never hosted India in any format under this arrangement.

https://x.com/BCCI/status/2087412098389467644

"We have hosted our home fixtures in both India and the UAE in recent years, and given the importance and scale of this series, we believe India provides an excellent setting for the event."

— Mirwais Ashraf, Afghanistan Cricket Board Chairman

BCCI president Mithun Manhas said India was committed to supporting the growth of cricket in Afghanistan. "We believe there is scope to do more together and will continue to support Afghanistan cricket while strengthening the relationship between the two cricketing nations," he said.

The BCCI mediated an understanding between the Afghanistan Cricket Board and the Delhi and District Cricket Association for the Arun Jaitley Stadium to serve as Afghanistan's home base, according to ESPN Cricinfo. The DDCA is scheduling its Delhi Premier League T20 around the series accordingly.

Schedule and Broadcasting

As things stand, the matches are slated for September 13, 15, and 17, though Cricbuzz reported that the dates remain somewhat tentative. If India's proposed white-ball tour to Bangladesh materializes — something that has gained renewed hope following the Indian government's invitation to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for the BRICS Summit — the Afghanistan series dates may need to shift by a few days.

There is limited room for a prolonged deferment. The Asian Games begin September 24, and India's home series against the West Indies starts September 27. Cricket is part of the Asian Games program, and BCCI selectors need to pick a 15-member T20 squad for the continental competition.

In a notable broadcast twist, the matches will not air on JioStar, the official broadcaster of India's home international games, since Afghanistan is the official host. Fancode holds the digital rights, while Zee and Sony Sports are the potential contenders for television rights. ITW Universe, the sports consulting firm coordinating with the ACB, is handling media and marketing.

Recent Form and Head-to-Head

India and Afghanistan last met in June, when India won a one-off Test by an innings and 300 runs and sealed a 3-0 sweep of the ODI series. In T20Is, India have won eight of nine meetings, with one match producing no result. The most dramatic encounter came in Bengaluru in January 2024, when both sides tied at 212 before India won the Super Over.

India's recent white-ball results have been mixed. After losing T20I series in Ireland and England this summer and going down 2-1 in the ODIs in England, the reigning T20 World Cup champions will look to reset before the Asian Games. Afghanistan, meanwhile, have not played any T20Is since the T20 World Cup earlier this year, where they won two of four games but missed out on a Super Eight spot.

What to Watch

For the Indian diaspora, the series offers a rare opportunity to watch India play an international series in Delhi during the September window. The arrangement also carries symbolic significance for Afghan cricket, demonstrating the strength of the BCCI-ACB relationship and Afghanistan's standing in international cricket despite the challenges at home. With the Asian Games looming, both squads will treat the series as high-stakes preparation for the continental showpiece.
